info.name: BloodLink API
info.description:
Every REST endpoint in the BloodLink backend (Spring Boot 4 / Java 25), grouped by module. Checked against the controllers at Stage 5 of the batch-stock work.

**Quick start.** The phone and password variables are pre-filled with the demo accounts, so start the backend in demo mode (see the README) and run the four **Login as …** requests in the Auth folder. Each saves a token (`donorToken`, `hospitalStaffToken`, `bankStaffToken`, `adminToken`) that every other request uses.

**Accounts.** Only donors register themselves (`POST /api/auth/register`). Hospital staff, blood bank staff and administrators are created by an administrator with **Admin > Users > Create Staff Account** (Business Rule 14), which returns a one-time **temporary** password. On an empty database with no administrator yet, start the backend with the four `BLOODLINK_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_*` settings (README, "Creating the first administrator"), or use demo mode.

**Temporary passwords (Business Rule 27).** An account an administrator created (and the first administrator) signs in with `user.mustChangePassword: true`. Until it changes its password with **My Account > Change My Password** (the temporary password as `currentPassword`), every other request gets 403 with `code: "PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED"`; only Get My Account, Change My Password and the public Auth requests still work, and the WebSocket refuses to connect. The change answers with a fresh token, which works normally straight after it.

**Who may change stock.** Only active blood bank staff, at their own bank: Add New Batch, Write Off Units, Record Donation and Contribute Units. An administrator gets 403 on all four (Business Rule 8); administrators can still read stock, batches and batch history, and may decline a request on a named bank's behalf.

**Blood groups in URLs.** In a path or query string, `+` must be written `%2B` (a raw `+` means a space). In a JSON body, write `O+` as normal. Every request below already does this.

**Error shape.** Every failure (400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 409, 500) returns `{ timestamp, status, error, code?, message, fieldErrors? }`. `fieldErrors` appears only for a validation failure and maps the field name to a message. `code` appears only on a refusal the client must act on: today, `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` (403, Business Rule 27) and `PASSWORD_CHANGED` (401: the token was issued before the account's password last changed, so sign in again; Business Rule 32).

**Forgot password (Business Rule 33).** Auth > Request Password Reset is public and always answers the same; administrators handle the result in Admin > Password Requests and reset with Users > Reset User Password.

**Real-time channel.** `/ws` (STOMP over SockJS) pushes all fourteen notification types to the user they are for, and only to active accounts. It is not a request/response endpoint, so it is not in this collection. Every push is also a stored notification, read with `GET /api/notifications`.

request.description: Public, unauthenticated. Returns `{"status":"ok"}` when the application is up.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Public: no token needed. Registration only ever creates a DONOR account. Sign-in, Register and Request Password Reset are rate limited (Business Rule 34): over a limit the answer is 429 with a `Retry-After` header in seconds and `{ "message": "Too many attempts. Please wait 15 minutes and try again." }`, stating the real time left. Sign-in: 3 failures per phone number in 15 minutes lock that number for 15 minutes, even for the correct password, and 30 failures per internet address in 15 minutes mean a 15-minute wait. Request Password Reset: 10 per address per hour. Register: 10 new accounts per address per hour.

request.description: Creates a donor and signs them in (201). `phone` is local (`076900005`) or international (`+232 76 900 005`) and is stored as `+232` plus 8 digits (Business Rule 13); a phone already registered is 409. `email` is optional: send `null` or leave it out (Business Rule 18). `bloodType` may be `null` if not known yet. `gender` is `MALE`, `FEMALE` or `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`. `password` follows the password rule (README): 8–72 characters with a capital letter, a small letter, a number and a special character (not a letter, number or whitespace); a weak one is 400 with `fieldErrors.password` naming what is missing, e.g. "Add a capital letter and a special character." Over 10 new accounts per internet address per hour: 429 with `Retry-After` (Business Rule 34). Saves the token to `donorToken`.

Signs in as the donor account in `donorPhone` and saves its token to `donorToken` (and its id to `donorUserId`). A wrong phone or password is 401; a suspended account is 403. The response's `user.mustChangePassword` is true for an account still on a temporary password (Business Rule 27).

exec: const roleKey = { DONOR: 'donor', HOSPITAL_STAFF: 'hospitalStaff', BLOOD_BANK_STAFF: 'bankStaff', ADMIN: 'admin' }[body.user.role];
pm.test('captured token for role ' + body.user.role, () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Signs in as the hospital staff account in `hospitalStaffPhone` and saves its token to `hospitalStaffToken` (and its id to `hospitalStaffUserId`). A wrong phone or password is 401; a suspended account is 403. The response's `user.mustChangePassword` is true for an account still on a temporary password (Business Rule 27).

exec: const roleKey = { DONOR: 'donor', HOSPITAL_STAFF: 'hospitalStaff', BLOOD_BANK_STAFF: 'bankStaff', ADMIN: 'admin' }[body.user.role];
pm.test('captured token for role ' + body.user.role, () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Signs in as the blood bank staff account in `bankStaffPhone` and saves its token to `bankStaffToken` (and its id to `bankStaffUserId`). A wrong phone or password is 401; a suspended account is 403. The response's `user.mustChangePassword` is true for an account still on a temporary password (Business Rule 27).

exec: const roleKey = { DONOR: 'donor', HOSPITAL_STAFF: 'hospitalStaff', BLOOD_BANK_STAFF: 'bankStaff', ADMIN: 'admin' }[body.user.role];
pm.test('captured token for role ' + body.user.role, () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Signs in as the admin account in `adminPhone` and saves its token to `adminToken` (and its id to `adminUserId`). A wrong phone or password is 401; a suspended account is 403. The response's `user.mustChangePassword` is true for an account still on a temporary password (Business Rule 27).

exec: const roleKey = { DONOR: 'donor', HOSPITAL_STAFF: 'hospitalStaff', BLOOD_BANK_STAFF: 'bankStaff', ADMIN: 'admin' }[body.user.role];
pm.test('captured token for role ' + body.user.role, () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Business Rule 33. Public: no token. `phone` is checked exactly as at sign-in (a malformed number is a 400 on `phone`). Every well-formed number then gets the same 202, `{ "message": "If this number is registered, an administrator will contact you." }`, never sooner than the minimum answer time (500 ms by default), whether it is unknown, suspended, already waiting or new. For an active account it records a waiting request and notifies every active administrator (PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED); asking again within an hour adds nothing, after an hour it re-alerts. It never resets a password. Over 10 requests per internet address per hour: 429 with `Retry-After` (Business Rule 34).

exec: pm.test('always the same answer', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('If this number is registered, an administrator will contact you.'));

request.description: Business Rule 33. Public: `{ phone }`, the support number the Sign in page shows after a request (`BLOODLINK_SUPPORT_PHONE`, as typed), or `null` when none is set.

item.name: My Account
item.description: Profile Settings for every role (Business Rule 16). Acts only on the caller's own account: the id comes from the token. Get My Account and Change My Password are the two requests an account on a temporary password may still make (Business Rule 27).

request.description: Any signed-in role. Name, email, phone, role and facility of the caller's own account. Includes `mustChangePassword`. Allowed even while the password must be changed (Business Rule 27).

Changes `fullName` and `email` only. Email is lower-cased and must be unique (409 if another account has it). A donor may send `null` to have no email; every other role must keep one. Any other field (phone, role, facility, status, anything unknown) is refused with a 400 naming it, and nothing is saved.

Needs the current password: a wrong one is 401 with a field error on `currentPassword` (this 401 does not sign the user out). `newPassword` follows the same password rule as registration (400 naming what is missing) and must differ from the current one (400). Success is 200 with a fresh token in the sign-in shape (`{ token, tokenType, expiresIn, user }`), saved to `donorToken`: every token issued before the change, this request's included, is then refused with 401 `code: "PASSWORD_CHANGED"` (Business Rule 32). Also how an account replaces its temporary password (Business Rule 27): send the temporary one as `currentPassword`; on success `mustChangePassword` becomes false and the fresh token works everywhere.

exec: pm.test('a fresh token replaces the old one', () => pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a('string'));

item.name: Donor (Self)
item.description: A donor's own profile and history, scoped by the token. DONOR (ADMIN is let through but has no donor profile).

request.description: Dashboard summary: blood type, eligibility (Business Rule 2), totals, first and last donation dates.
Every donation, newest first. Each row's `bloodType` is the group tested at that donation (Business Rule 4).

item.name: Donor Lookup (Blood Bank)
item.description: Finding a donor by phone before recording a donation. Active BLOOD_BANK_STAFF only (Business Rule 8).

request.description: Active blood bank staff only: ADMIN, hospital staff and donors get 403, the same as Record Donation (Business Rule 8). Exact match only, typed either way (local or `+232`). 404 if nobody matches. Saves the donor id to `donorLookupId` for Record Donation.

item.name: Donor Roster (Blood Bank)
item.description: Donors who have given at least one donation at the caller's bank (Business Rule 21). BLOOD_BANK_STAFF for their own bank; an ADMIN must name the bank with `bloodBankId`. No address, email or date of birth is ever returned.

query.description: Name or part of a phone number
Required for ADMIN; ignored for bank staff

request.description: One page of the roster: `{ content, page, size, totalElements, totalPages }`. A bad parameter is a 400 naming it, never corrected. Tick the optional filters to try them. Saves the first donor's id to `rosterDonorId`.

item.name: Get Donor's Donations at This Bank

query.description: Required for ADMIN; ignored for bank staff

request.description: That donor's donations at this bank only, newest first, at most 50. A donor with no donation here is a 404, the same as an unknown id.

Business Rule 28: set or correct a donor's profile blood group after a test, with no donation. Active blood bank staff of any bank, for any donor; ADMIN, hospital staff and donors get 403. `bloodType` is one of the eight groups; `note` (how or where the test was done) is required, at most 500 characters. The same group as now is a 400 on `bloodType`. Answers 200 with `{ donorId, fullName, previousBloodType, bloodType }` and writes a DONOR_BLOOD_GROUP_UPDATED audit entry carrying the note.

item.name: Blood Banks
item.description: Blood banks are created by an administrator (Admin > Facilities). The list is open to any signed-in role; the dashboard is for bank staff and administrators.

request.description: Any signed-in role. Every blood bank, for pickers and display.
BLOOD_BANK_STAFF or ADMIN. The dashboard stat cards: usable units, donations this month, open requests (pending and partly filled) and registered donors.

item.name: Hospitals
item.description: Hospitals are created by an administrator (Admin > Facilities).

request.description: Any signed-in role.

item.name: Inventory
item.description: Stock is held batch by batch, each batch with its own expiry date (Business Rule 24). Only usable units (not expired) are counted. Reading totals is open to any signed-in role; batch lists and history are for that bank's staff and administrators; changing stock is for that bank's active staff only, and an ADMIN gets 403.

request.description: Always all eight blood groups. Per group: usable units, status (Critical under 15, Low under 40, else Sufficient), the earliest usable expiry date, units expiring within 28 days, expired units awaiting write-off, the number of batches, and the Send Appeal state.
Usable units, units expiring within 28 days, expired units awaiting write-off, groups at Critical, units issued this month, and the Sufficient/Low/Critical breakdown.

Creates a new batch with its own expiry date; nothing is merged. `unitsToAdd` is 1–1000. `expiryDate` must be today or later and at most 365 days away (400 otherwise). The blood group in the path is URL-encoded (`O%2B` is O+). Own bank only (403 for another bank's id). ADMIN: 403.

The bank's batches that still hold units, expired ones included, grouped by blood group and then earliest expiry first. Each shows units received and remaining, expiry date, state (USABLE, EXPIRING_SOON or EXPIRED), days to expiry and source (DONATION, MANUAL or MIGRATED). That bank's staff or ADMIN; hospitals and donors get 403. Saves the first batch's id to `batchId`.
One batch as it stands, plus where its units went: issues to hospital requests and write-offs (who, when, why). That bank's staff or ADMIN. A batch of another bank asked for under this bank is a 404.

Takes units off one batch and records why (201). `units` is 1 up to what is left; more is a 409 naming what is left. `reason` is `EXPIRED`, `DAMAGED`, `FAILED_TESTING`, `DATA_ENTRY_ERROR` or `OTHER`. `note` is optional (500 characters at most) but required for `OTHER`. Expired batches can be written off. Recorded in the audit log as STOCK_WRITTEN_OFF; cannot be undone. Own bank's active staff only; ADMIN: 403.

item.name: Blood Requests
item.description: Hospitals raise requests; any blood bank with stock contributes units until the request is covered (Business Rule 20). Status is PENDING, PARTIALLY_FULFILLED, FULFILLED or REJECTED, worked out from the contributions.

request.description: HOSPITAL_STAFF only (201). The caller's own hospital is stamped on by the server. `urgencyLevel` is `ROUTINE`, `URGENT` or `EMERGENCY`. `unitsRequested` is 1–500. `patientReference` is optional, 255 characters at most. Saves the new id to `bloodRequestId`.

Hospital staff see their own hospital's requests, with how many units have arrived and from which banks. Switch the token to `{{bankStaffToken}}` for a bank's view: every request with units outstanding that the bank has not declined, plus requests it has contributed to.

item.name: List Requests (as Admin, for one bank)

request.description: `bloodBankId` shows one bank's view. It matters only for ADMIN (or bank staff with no bank yet); assigned staff always see their own bank.

Issues units from the caller's bank to the request, earliest-expiring batch first, and updates its status. Units above what is still outstanding are capped, not refused. More than the bank's usable stock is a 409 naming the usable and expired units. A bank that declined cannot contribute (409). Active bank staff only, acting as their own bank; ADMIN: 403.

This bank cannot help (Business Rule 11). The request leaves this bank's queue only and stays open for the others; it becomes REJECTED only when every bank has declined an untouched (PENDING) request. Declining twice, or after contributing, is a 409. Bank staff act as their own bank (`bloodBankId` ignored). An ADMIN may decline on a bank's behalf by giving `bloodBankId`.

Business Rule 35. Active staff of the hospital that made the request, while it is PENDING or PARTIALLY_FULFILLED. `reason` is NO_LONGER_NEEDED, PATIENT_TRANSFERRED, OBTAINED_ELSEWHERE, ENTERED_BY_MISTAKE or OTHER (400 on `reason` otherwise); `note` is optional, at most 200 characters, and required for OTHER (400 on `note`). Answers 200 with the request. Units already supplied stay supplied and no stock returns. Fully supplied, rejected or already cancelled: 409. Another hospital's request: 404, like a missing one. Bank staff, donors and ADMIN: 403. Active staff of every bank still watching the request get a REQUEST_CANCELLED notification; banks that declined do not.

item.name: Appeals
item.description: A blood bank asking eligible donors of one group to come in (Business Rules 1, 2 and 12). BLOOD_BANK_STAFF and ADMIN.

request.description: Sends nothing. How many active, eligible donors an appeal for this group would reach, and how many are held back inside the 90-day recovery window. Suspended donors are counted in neither.

Notifies every active, eligible donor of the group (201) with a receipt of how many were notified and skipped. `note` is optional, 280 characters at most. Bank staff act as their own bank; an ADMIN must give `bloodBankId`.

Refused with 409 when the bank has 30 or more usable units of the group (no shortage), or when a recent appeal's cooldown is still running: 5 hours if it was sent under 15 units, 24 hours if under 30. The cooldown ends early once stock climbs back over that level.

item.name: Donation Bookings
item.description: Business Rule 29: an active donor who is eligible today books one donation visit at a time (blood bank, date from today to today + 30 in UTC, MORNING or AFTERNOON). A booking never changes stock. Recording a donation closes it (ATTENDED at that bank, otherwise CANCELLED); the daily 06:00 UTC job marks past ones MISSED and sends the donor one reminder: the day before, or on the day if that was missed. Suspending a donor cancels their open booking.

request.description: DONOR only (any other role 403). Change `bookingDate` to a date from today to today + 30. 201 with the booking; the bank's active staff get DONATION_BOOKED. 409 if the donor is not eligible today (it names the date they may book from) or already has an open booking; 400 on `bookingDate` outside the window, on `timeOfDay` other than MORNING/AFTERNOON; 404 for an unknown bank.
The donor's open booking dated today or later, or 204 No Content when there is none.
Cancels the donor's own open booking while its date is today or later; the bank's active staff get DONATION_BOOKING_CANCELLED. 404 when there is none, 409 once its date has passed.

The caller's own bank's BOOKED visits dated today or later, by date then morning first: `{ id, bookingDate, timeOfDay, donorName, bloodType }` (`bloodType` null when not recorded). Active blood bank staff only; ADMIN, hospital staff and donors 403.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: The stored side of the bell: every notification is a row, whether or not it was also pushed live. Notifications only ever go to active accounts.

request.description: Any signed-in role. The 50 most recent, newest first. Saves the first id to `notificationId`; with a donor token it also saves the first appeal not yet accepted to `appealNotificationId`.
The bell's badge number.
Marks every unread notification of the caller as read.
Run List My Notifications first. Someone else's notification is a 404, not a 403.

DONOR only (Business Rule 25). Run List My Notifications with `{{donorToken}}` first. Marks the appeal accepted and read, and tells the sending bank's active staff. Safe to repeat: the staff are told once. Refused with 409 if the donor is not eligible; another user's notification, or one that is not an appeal, is a 404. Accepting books nothing; the donation is still recorded by bank staff.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Every route here requires ADMIN (any other role 403, no token 401).

item.name: Users
item.description: Staff and administrator accounts (Business Rules 14, 17 and 22). Every change is written to the audit log.

query.description: Name, email, or part of a phone number

request.description: One page of accounts: `{ content, page, size, totalElements, totalPages }`. A bad parameter is a 400 naming it. No password hash is ever returned. Saves the first account that is not the caller's own to `otherUserId`.

Creates a HOSPITAL_STAFF, BLOOD_BANK_STAFF or ADMIN account (201); DONOR is refused. `bloodBankId` is required for BLOOD_BANK_STAFF and forbidden otherwise; `hospitalId` the same for HOSPITAL_STAFF; ADMIN takes neither. Email is required. A phone or email already in use is a 409. The response holds `temporaryPassword`, shown this once only. It is temporary: the new account must replace it at its first sign-in before it can do anything else (Business Rule 27). Saves the new account's id to `otherUserId`.

Changes another account's phone and facility. Send the full wanted state: the phone, plus the facility the account's role needs (this example suits a blood bank staff account). Role cannot be changed (400), nor the caller's own account (409). A phone already in use is a 409.

Business Rule 31: gives another account a new temporary password (meeting the password rule) and answers 200 with `{ account, temporaryPassword }`, sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. This is the only time the password is readable; only its hash is stored, so the old password stops working at once. The account must choose its own password at its next sign-in (`mustChangePassword`). No body. Your own account is a 409 (use Profile Settings); another administrator may be reset; a suspended account stays suspended. Audited as `ADMIN_PASSWORD_RESET`, and an active holder gets a `PASSWORD_RESET_BY_ADMIN` notification; neither contains the password. Every token the holder already had is refused at once (401 `PASSWORD_CHANGED`, Business Rule 32); yours is unaffected. Non-admin tokens 403, no token 401, unknown id 404.
Takes effect at once: the account's token is refused on its next request, and it receives no notifications. An administrator cannot suspend their own account (409).
Reverses a suspension. `status` is `ACTIVE` or `SUSPENDED`.

item.name: Password Requests
item.description: Business Rule 33: "Forgot password?" requests from the Sign in page. Administrators only (other roles 403, no token 401). Resetting the password itself is Users > Reset User Password, which also closes the account's waiting request (resolution RESET).

request.description: One page of WAITING (default) or DONE requests: waiting newest asked first, done most recently handled first. Each item: `id`, `account` (the User Accounts shape, so the Manage box can open), `requestedAt`, `status`, `resolution` (RESET / CLOSED, null while waiting), `handledById`, `handledByName`, `handledAt`, `note`. Saves the first id to `passwordRequestId`. A bad `status`, `page` or `size` is a 400.
`{ waiting }`: the Admin Console's menu badge and User Accounts banner.

Closes a waiting request without a reset: status DONE, resolution CLOSED, audited as PASSWORD_REQUEST_CLOSED. `note` is optional (blank is none), at most 200 characters (400 on `note`). Already done is a 409, an unknown id a 404. The body may be left out.

item.name: Facilities
item.description: Adding blood banks and hospitals (Business Rule 19). Create only: there is no edit or delete.

request.description: 201 with the new bank. All three fields are required. The name is unique among blood banks, ignoring case and extra spaces (409). `contactPhone` is stored as typed. The bank starts with no stock.
201 with the new hospital. Same rules as Create Blood Bank; a hospital may share a name with a blood bank.

One page of the permanent audit log, newest first: account creation, edits, suspensions and reactivations, facility creation, and stock write-offs by bank staff (Business Rule 17). Read-only: any other method is 405.

item.name: Reports
item.description: Read-only figures, counted by the database. No donor's personal details appear anywhere (Business Rule 23).

request.description: Donations per month for the last six months, oldest first, empty months included (the Dashboard chart).
Citywide request counts: pending, partly filled, fulfilled and rejected, plus the total (the Dashboard donut).
`{ total, donors, hospitalStaff, bloodBankStaff, admins }` (the Dashboard cards and role buttons).

Citywide usable units per blood group with Critical/Low/Sufficient status, each bank's total and its Critical and Low group counts, units expiring within 28 days, and expired units awaiting write-off (shown, never counted as stock). As of today.

Requests created in the range, by status, blood group and urgency, the fulfilment rate (null when nothing was decided) and how many were filled by more than one bank. Default range: the 1st of the month five months back until today. A bad date, `from` after `to`, or more than five years is a 400.
Donations in the range per month, per blood bank and per tested blood group. Same range rules as Requests Summary.
Total donors, eligible now, in recovery, and per blood group (plus Unknown). As of today.
The Stock Summary as a CSV file. Use Postman's Send and Download.
The Requests Summary as a CSV file. Same range rules.
The Donations Summary as a CSV file. Same range rules.
The Donors Summary as a CSV file.

item.name: Donations
item.description: Recording a donation: a Donation row, the donor's last-donation date and a new stock batch, in one action. Active BLOOD_BANK_STAFF only; ADMIN gets 403 (Business Rule 8).

request.description: Run Look Up Donor by Phone first. `bloodType` is the group as tested today, always stated (Business Rule 4). `unitsDonated` is 1–10. `expiryDate` is optional: leave it `null` for donation date + 42 days, or give the bag label's date (today to 365 days ahead). The donor must be eligible: a donor inside the 90-day recovery window is a 409 and nothing is written. The donation is recorded at the caller's own bank, dated today. Business Rule 28: the donor's profile group follows the test. An empty profile group is set to it; a different one is replaced only with `confirmBloodGroupChange: true` — without it the answer is a 409 with `code: "BLOOD_GROUP_CHANGE_UNCONFIRMED"` and nothing is written, not even the donation. Every profile change is audited; the receipt's `profileBloodTypeUpdated` says whether one happened. Business Rule 29: the donor's open donation visit, if any, is closed too — ATTENDED if it was at this bank, otherwise CANCELLED and the booked bank told.

variable.description: The shared demo password, public, demo data only.
A number no account has yet, for Register (Donor).
Demo hospital staff, Makeni Regional Hospital.
Demo blood bank staff, Makeni Regional Blood Bank.
Makeni Regional Blood Bank — seeded, fixed id (V4).
Holy Spirit Blood Bank — seeded, fixed id (V4).
Makeni Regional Hospital — seeded, fixed id (V6).
Holy Spirit Hospital — seeded, fixed id (V6).
Set by List My Notifications run with the donor token.
Set by Look Up Donor by Phone (for Record Donation).
Set by List Users or Create Staff Account.
